subject: FinWise - Load test coordination & SLO confirmation
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: FinWise - Load test coordination & SLO confirmation

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Recap (what we heard)
- SLO targets you called out: 99th percentile latency <= 200ms for text generation, steady-state throughput ~600 req/s, concurrency target ~50 active sessions.
- Streaming: some flows will use server-streaming for partial responses (chat-like). We confirmed that streaming must maintain per-token latency under 50ms where possible.
- Test goals: validate that our production routing meets your SLOs under a realistic traffic profile, and identify any degradation points.

Next steps (customer-led load test)
1) You run a customer-led load test using your preferred tooling (k6/Locust).
2) We provide test accounts, IP allowlist ranges, and a short checklist for recommended ramps and monitoring metrics.
3) We’ll have Redwood infra/CS on-call during the window to watch dashboards and assist.

Please confirm: preferred test dates/windows, whether you’ll use k6 or Locust (or both), and if you can share your scripts so we can sanity-check the traffic pattern. If you’d like, Marissa (CC) will provide the allowlist and a test credential.

Suggested ramp: 5 min warmup to 100rps, 15 min linear ramp to 600rps, 30 min soak, then a few sudden bursts up to 1,000rps to exercise autoscaling/fallbacks.

Thanks — happy to refine based on your needs.

—
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Logan — great call. We’ll run the customer-led test and can do either k6 or Locust; engineers prefer k6 for scripting but we have a Locust harness as well.

Availability: we can run an initial test window on Monday 2026-12-06 23:00 UTC (overnight for our production traffic) and a follow-up on Tuesday 2026-12-07 23:00 UTC if needed.

Attaching our current k6 script (this ramps per your suggestion and includes the streaming workload emulation). Please review for anything that would generate unrealistic load against your infra.

Attachments: k6_load_test_v2.js (JavaScript, 18KB)

Questions for Redwood:
- What IP ranges should we allow from your side?
- Can you provision a test API key/tenant with 1,000 qps throttle so we can validate throttling behavior?
- Any recommended metrics/graphs to watch on your console during the run?

I’ve CC’d our ops mailbox — they’ll handle test execution and any follow-ups.

Regards,
Jordan Smith
Principal SRE | FinWise
jordan.smith@finwise.com

Date: 2026-12-01T12:40:00-08:00

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for sending the k6 script. Quick responses below and what we’ve provisioned on our side: 

1) IP allowlist: please allow the following egress ranges (Redwood control plane / test agents): 34.82.0.0/15, 35.192.0.0/12, and our CDN edge 3.210.0.0/16. If you need CIDR-minified lists for firewall rules, say the word and I’ll export them.

2) Test account: we created a temporary test tenant and API key for FinWise: tenant id FW-LIVE-TEST-01 and API key attached in a CSV (test-user-credentials.csv). Key expires 2026-12-09. Use the header Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>.

3) Throttles: we’ve set a soft throttle at 1,000 qps on the test tenant so you can safely spike; Redwood will return 429 when throttled — please capture those responses in your run.

4) Recommended metrics: 50/95/99/99.9 latency percentiles, token-per-second throughput, CPU/GPU utilization per host, queue/backlog length, and streaming partial-response times. We’ll share a dashboard link; quick link below.

Dashboard (read-only): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/fw-loadtest-fw-live-test-01

Attachments: test-user-credentials.csv (CSV, 0.8KB)

I’ll also drop the CIDR list to the shared Drive folder in case your network team prefers that. We’ll plan to have a Redwood on-call SRE + CS during the test window.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

- Rishi: can you watch the infra dashboard (GPU/CPU, queue depth) and be ready to scale nodes if we see queue/backlog > 5s?

I attached a quick locust-based sanity test that we can run from our staging agents if we want to reproduce the script shape locally before the customer run.
